subChunks.title: Reading & Writing Files (NIO.2)

storyBeats.text: Eldrin opens the Academy's scroll archive and begins reading from a magical tome that connects to the physical scroll rack on the wall.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: File I/O is your application's memory beyond the session. Without it, every run starts fresh. With it, spells persist, logs accumulate, configurations endure. The NIO.2 API — Files and Path — is the modern way.

storyBeats.label: Read and write

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Always use try-with-resources when working with streams or readers. The file handle closes automatically when the block exits — even if an exception is thrown. A forgotten open file handle is a resource leak.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Write a list of three lines to a temp file, read them back, and print the line count then each line.
guidedPractice.hint: Use Files.createTempFile(), Files.write(), Files.readAllLines(), then Files.delete() to clean up.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between Files.readAllLines() and using a BufferedReader. When would you prefer each?

questions.prompt: What is the main advantage of try-with-resources when doing file I/O?
options: Resources are automatically closed even if an exception occurs
questions.answer: Resources are automatically closed even if an exception occurs
questions.explanation: Try-with-resources calls close() automatically on any AutoCloseable resource, ensuring file handles are never leaked — even when exceptions are thrown.

subChunks.title: Paths, File Operations & Serialisation

storyBeats.text: Eldrin seals an entire Wizard object inside a magical crystal for transport to another academy — the serialised form persists the object's complete state.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Serialisation is object teleportation — you freeze an object's state to a byte stream, ship it across a network or to disk, and reconstruct it identically on the other end. It requires the Serializable marker contract.

storyBeats.label: Serialise and deserialise

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: In modern applications, JSON has largely replaced native serialisation for data exchange — it's human-readable, language-agnostic, and more robust to class changes. But Java serialisation remains useful for internal caching and RMI.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Serialise a simple Wizard object (name, level) to a temp file, then deserialise and print its fields.
guidedPractice.hint: The Wizard class must implement Serializable. Use ObjectOutputStream to write, ObjectInputStream to read.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What is Java object serialisation? What interface must a class implement to be serialised, and what is serialVersionUID for?

questions.prompt: What interface must a Java class implement to be serialisable?
questions.explanation: Serializable is a marker interface (no methods) that signals to the JVM that a class's instances can be serialised to a byte stream.

questions.prompt: Fields marked transient in a serialisable class are saved to the byte stream.
questions.explanation: transient fields are explicitly excluded from serialisation — useful for sensitive data (passwords) or fields that cannot be serialised (threads, streams).
